title: Land a job only on the branch it was dispatched from
summary: Landing (`land::plan`, called at run.rs ~1540 and ~1778) only checks that the job's base is an ancestor of the current HEAD, so a job can land on any branch checked out when it finishes. The change records or reads the dispatch branch and, when the current branch differs, makes the job stale or blocked, with nothing landed and a clear reason. The audience is the Athena user running jobs while switching branches.

defaults_applied.how: Add unit tests in land.rs or landing_tests.rs for same-branch and other-branch landings; cargo test and clippy stay clean.
Put the check in the shared landing decision so every landing path enforces it, not just one caller.
A test with real git switches branches after dispatch, where the base is still an ancestor, and shows nothing lands.
One focused change to the landing decision and its callers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The dispatch branch is already captured at dispatch (run.rs ~1405 reads current_branch into a record); the fix reuses it rather than adding new storage. This is unverified: I read only part of that code.
A mismatch refuses the landing and leaves the job stale (or blocked) with a reason naming both branches. Nothing is committed on the wrong branch.
A detached HEAD at dispatch is compared as 'no branch'. It lands only if the finish is also detached, and the commit is the same as before.
The landing retry path (run.rs ~1778) gets the same check as the main path (~1540).

acceptance_criteria.text: Run `cargo test`. A new test dispatches a job on branch A, switches to branch B (which contains the base commit), finishes the job, and shows that it does not land on B (B's tip is unchanged) and its outcome is stale or blocked with a reason naming the dispatch branch.

Run `cargo test`. A test shows a job still lands normally, as a fast-forward of the branch, when the checked-out branch at finish is the one it was dispatched from, including the records-only-changes replay case.
Run `cargo test`. The landing-retry-after-blocked path also refuses when the current branch differs from the dispatch branch.
The header comment of land.rs (the design §7.3 pseudocode) states the new rule that the branch must equal the dispatch branch, so a reader can see the rule.
Run `cargo clippy` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean, and the existing land and landing tests still pass.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry stating that jobs now land only on their dispatch branch.

out_of_scope: Changing how PR-based landing or resync_onto_merge picks its branch
Changing the stale-detection rules for governed content
Governance files such as athena.toml and defaults.toml
departures: Slightly higher cost and time than the reference: the fix touches the core landing path and needs tests that switch branches with real git.
